NSE had received a No Objection Certificate from SEBI in January 2026, clearing a major hurdle for its proposed listing. NSE’s board approved the IPO in February, while the exchange filed a 614-page Draft Red Herring Prospectus in June. The proposed issue is entirely an offer-for-sale of up to 148.9 million shares, or nearly 6% of NSE’s equity. Based on its then-prevailing unlisted-market valuation, the IPO was estimated at around ₹30,000 crore. The approval timeline was extended after NSE filed an addendum to its DRHP following a change in selling shareholders. Public comments on the IPO are now open until August 31. Until now, Kite users could view mutual funds but were redirected to the separate Coin app to make investments. The upcoming integration will allow investors to manage more of their equity and mutual fund investments from a single platform. Zerodha also plans to let customers import mutual fund holdings from other platforms into Kite. The move marks a shift from Zerodha’s long-standing strategy of separating active investing on Kite from passive, long-term investing on Coin. However, the company says Coin will continue to remain its passive-focused platform. With more than 3 million mutual fund investors and 5.6 million SIP accounts, Zerodha is looking to strengthen its position in the increasingly competitive mutual fund market. The integration could also make mutual fund investing more accessible to Kite’s large user base.

articles.title: ‘Expect A Bigger & Broader Market Move Now’: Why Stronger Growth & Earnings Could Trigger FII Return
articles.summary: Indian markets could be heading towards a broader and stronger phase as improving economic indicators, rising industrial production, accelerating bank credit and a revival in corporate earnings point to a potential inflection in the growth cycle. Abhay Laijawala, Chief Investment Officer, India at Lighthouse Canton says the combination of stronger economic growth and earnings upgrades could eventually bring foreign investors back to Indian equities. He expects the economy to move towards 8% real GDP growth, translating into 12-13% nominal GDP growth and potentially 16-18% corporate earnings growth. He sees continued strength in midcaps and smallcaps, with largecaps likely to participate as foreign flows return. On sectors, auto ancillaries and paints remain preferred, while IT services are on the radar but await a recovery in revenue growth. With the festive season approaching, the key question is whether improving fundamentals can trigger a broader market move.
